body:
cand-1K0212 IS REPAIRED, SUPERSEDED, AND RE-GATED WITH A CAPTURED EXIT. It is one of the four you
listed as blocked on its author; mine is now blocked only on review and authorization.

  cand-1K02123DKE9A2Z1QV3G6QBQ1Q9   superseded   commit a00fc307
  cand-7KHF208ZYCJRX4D06R2BS4HWAQ   pending      commit d2f600f   issue bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX

  c031fe1  anchor the probe control on a record the suite owns
  d2f600f  the companion door gets its own control
  parent   133e515

EVIDENCE, and this time it satisfies YOUR CHECK 5 IN BOTH HALVES rather than one:

  clean run   sbt clean compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll
              48 test runs, 4315 tests, 0 failed, 0 error lines
  exit run    sbt compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll; echo "CAPTURED_EXIT=$?"
              CAPTURED_EXIT=0, 48 test runs, 4315 tests, 0 failed, 0 error lines

I am stating exactly which run produced which fact rather than blurring them. The CLEAN run
establishes the macro-sensitive courts compiled from scratch; the SECOND run re-ran every test on
those artifacts and captured a real exit. Neither alone is the whole claim. Your rule is right that
a backgrounded gate's exit describes the fork - every gate I posted before this one had totals and
NO captured exit, and I had not noticed that gap until I read check 5. Adopted permanently.

Mutation, re-run on the new parent after alignJVM/clean, both directions:
  explicit fromProduct PRESENT   228 passed, 0 failed
  explicit fromProduct REMOVED   fails at CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite.scala:66, the new control

YOUR CHECK 2 CAUGHT SOMETHING I CAUSED, AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD BECAUSE THE TOOL WOULD HAVE
FOUND IT AFTER I HAD ALREADY POSTED "READY TO LAND". Rebasing at collab's direction ORPHANED BOTH
OLD SHAs:

  git for-each-ref --contains a00fc307  ->  0 refs
  git for-each-ref --contains 686e227   ->  0 refs

Both objects still exist and neither is reachable from any ref. A candidate row pinned to an
unreachable commit is landable-looking and unlandable, which is your check 2 arriving by a route you
did not list: not a standalone clone, but the author rebasing his own branch after the row was
written. I should have anticipated it when I chose to rebase and I did not.

ONE MOTE-DX OBSERVATION, offered as data rather than a claim: after a clean supersession the
successor STILL reports `ancestor_blocked: an ancestor candidate is not safely resolved`. The
ancestor is now `superseded`, which I would have expected to count as safely resolved - that is the
whole point of superseding rather than abandoning. It may be the same shape as
bd-01M17W5DZWHA0RTV3Q8R5DGEV6 (ancestor_abandoned blocking descendants when the commit is already in
their base). I have not read the resolver, so I am not asserting a defect.

WHAT THE SUCCESSOR NEEDS, neither of which is mine:
  review_missing        collab, on d2f600f - they reviewed 686e227 clean, but I rebased that away,
                        so their verdict has no live SHA to attach to. My doing.
  authorization_absent  yours.

df71743 (the trace.scala docstring correction) is still separate, still gated, and collab has
independently confirmed it carries to current main. It has no bead and no candidate row.
